concepts.name: Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ): Rights, Limits, and Overlaps
key_dimensions: UNCLOS definition: 200 nautical miles from baseline vs. territorial sea (12 NM) vs. contiguous zone (24 NM) — common confusion point
Sovereign rights vs. full sovereignty distinction (resource exploitation rights ≠ territorial control)
Overlapping EEZ disputes: India-Sri Lanka, India-Maldives, South China Sea — geopolitical implications
India's EEZ area (~2.37 million sq km) and its resource potential including fisheries, hydrocarbons, and deep-sea minerals

concepts.name: Continental Shelf: Legal vs. Geological Definition and Extended Claims
key_dimensions: UNCLOS Article 76: Legal shelf up to 200 NM vs. geological shelf — difference between the two
Extended Continental Shelf (ECS) claims beyond 200 NM up to 350 NM — CLCS submission process
India's ECS submission and Bay of Bengal/Arabian Sea claims
Resources on the continental shelf: oil, gas, polymetallic nodules — sovereign rights of coastal states

concepts.name: Polymetallic Nodules: Composition, Distribution, and Deep-Sea Mining Governance
key_dimensions: Composition: manganese, nickel, cobalt, copper, iron — strategic mineral significance for clean energy transition
Concentration zones: Clarion-Clipperton Zone (Pacific), Central Indian Ocean Basin (CIOB) — India's allocated site

concepts.name: Hydrothermal Vents and Polymetallic Sulphides: Resource and Ecological Significance

Mineral richness: copper, zinc, gold, silver sulphides — distinction from polymetallic nodules
Unique chemosynthetic ecosystems — biodiversity hotspot vs. mining conflict

concepts.name: Cobalt-Rich Ferromanganese Crusts: Occurrence and Strategic Value
key_dimensions: Found on seamounts and ridges at 400–7000m depth — distinct from nodules found on abyssal plains
High cobalt content — critical mineral for EV batteries and strategic reserves
ISA exploration regulations and India's interest in Indo-Pacific seamounts
Comparison with polymetallic nodules: depth, mining difficulty, and mineral profile — UPSC trap area

concepts.name: Gas Hydrates (Methane Clathrates): Distribution, Potential, and Environmental Risks
key_dimensions: Formation conditions: high pressure + low temperature — continental slopes and polar regions
India's Krishna-Godavari Basin as a major hydrate reserve — National Gas Hydrate Program (NGHP)
Energy potential: estimated to exceed all conventional fossil fuel reserves combined
Environmental risk: methane release and climate feedback loop — destabilization during extraction

concepts.name: Ocean Fisheries: Zones, Types, and Sustainable Management Frameworks
key_dimensions: Pelagic vs. demersal fisheries — geographic distribution and species significance

concepts.name: Mangroves as Marine Resources: Ecological Services and Threats
key_dimensions: Carbon sequestration: 'blue carbon' storage capacity — higher than terrestrial forests per unit area
Coastal protection, nursery habitat for fisheries, and livelihood support — multi-dimensional services
India's mangrove cover: Sundarbans (largest), distribution along coasts — state-wise data
Threats: aquaculture expansion, urbanization, climate change-induced sea-level rise — policy responses (Wetlands Rules, 2017; CAMPA)

concepts.name: Coral Reefs: Distribution, Biodiversity Role, and Bleaching Phenomenon
key_dimensions: Types: fringing, barrier, atoll — formation and geographic examples (Great Barrier Reef, Lakshadweep, Gulf of Mannar)
Coral bleaching: mechanism (zooxanthellae expulsion due to thermal stress) vs. coral death — distinction
Economic value: fisheries, tourism, coastal protection — quantification and policy relevance
Global and Indian initiatives: Coral Triangle Initiative, Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve, IUCN Red List coral status

concepts.name: Seaweed and Marine Bio-Resources: Economic and Pharmaceutical Potential
key_dimensions: Types: red, brown, green algae — industrial uses (agar, carrageenan, alginates)
Pharmaceutical potential: bioactive compounds from marine organisms — blue biotechnology

concepts.name: Deep Ocean Mission (India): Objectives, Components, and Strategic Significance
key_dimensions: Five major components: deep-sea mining, ocean climate change advisory, deep ocean survey, advanced marine station, ocean biology — coverage breadth

concepts.name: Blue Economy: Definition, Pillars, and India's Policy Framework
key_dimensions: Definition: sustainable use of ocean resources for economic growth — distinction from traditional maritime economy

concepts.name: International Seabed Authority (ISA): Mandate, Structure, and 'Area' Governance
key_dimensions: Established under UNCLOS 1982 / 1994 Agreement — headquarters in Kingston, Jamaica
Concept of 'The Area' as common heritage of mankind — no state sovereignty, ISA manages on behalf of all states

Draft Mining Code negotiations — environmental safeguards, developing country benefit-sharing — current controversy

concepts.name: UNCLOS (Law of the Sea): Maritime Zones Hierarchy and Key Provisions
key_dimensions: Zone hierarchy: Internal waters → Territorial Sea → Contiguous Zone → EEZ → Continental Shelf → High Seas — rights differ in each

concepts.name: Offshore Hydrocarbons: Indian Basins, Extraction Technology, and Governance

concepts.name: Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC): Principle, Potential, and Limitations
key_dimensions: Working principle: temperature difference between surface (warm) and deep water (cold) — minimum 20°C differential needed
Geographic suitability: tropical oceans — India's potential sites (Lakshadweep, Andaman)

concepts.name: Tidal and Wave Energy: Resource Potential and India-Specific Context
key_dimensions: Tidal energy: gravitational forces of moon/sun — barrage vs. tidal stream technology; Gulf of Kutch and Khambhat potential
Wave energy: driven by wind — distribution pattern (higher latitude coasts have higher potential)

concepts.name: Marine Protected Areas (MPAs): Types, Governance, and India's Coverage

concepts.name: BBNJ Agreement (High Seas Treaty, 2023): Key Provisions and Significance
key_dimensions: Full form: Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction — adopted under UNCLOS framework

concepts.name: Desalination: Technology, Energy Demand, and Marine Environmental Impact
